keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Hazaraspids). The page says they 'ruled the Zagros Mountains region of southwestern Iran, essentially in Lorestan' from Idaj; the Khorshidi page assigns 'Little Lorestan' (capital Khorramabad) to the Khorshidis and speaks of a neighbouring line 'who ruled over Greater Lorestan' (read here as the Hazaraspids), so the modern Lorestan province is left to the khorshidi-dynasty dossier and the Bakhtiari country with a disc at Idaj is drawn here. The page gives no frontier and says Abu Tahir 'extended his realm as far as Isfahan' (undated; not drawn).

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Three pages opened (Hazaraspids, Khorshidi dynasty, Lorestan Province, the last unusable), within budget. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Territory: the Hazaraspids page says 'essentially in Lorestan' with the capital at Idaj (Izeh, in Khuzestan) and no frontier; the Khorshidi page assigns Little Lorestan (Khorramabad) to the Khorshidis and mentions a neighbouring line 'who ruled over Greater Lorestan' (read as the Hazaraspids), so this dossier draws the Bakhtiari country with a disc at Idaj and leaves the Lorestan province to khorshidi-dynasty. The reading is mine; if the reviewer prefers the page's 'Lorestan', the two dossiers overlap in the province.
Status (suzerain-side events not recorded here): infobox 'Vassal of the Ilkhanate (1256-1335)' (ulus-of-hulegu) and 'Vassal of Timurid Empire (1393-1424)' (timurid-empire); Yusuf Shah I 'received Ilkhan Abaqa's confirmation of his rule'; Afrasiab I 'reinstated by Ilkhan Gaykhatu but executed by Gazan in October 1296'; the page also says a Hazaraspid army was defeated by the Mongols 'at Kuhrud near Kashan' (undated, ruler not named).
Ruler table: the page's table is inconsistent (Abu Tahir 1115-1153, Yusuf Shah I listed twice, '1023-1153' and '1274-1288'); the strip omits the first Yusuf Shah entry and the years 1153-1204, which the extract does not give.
Not settled: the year of the Isfahan reach (Abu Tahir), of the Yusuf Shah I additions (undated within 1274-1288), of the Yusuf Shah II annexations (first half of the 14th century), of the Muzaffarid occupation of Idaj; the infobox predecessors 'Salghurids; Shabankara'; the Timurid conquest of 1393 (infobox status date only).
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Idaj (Izeh) and Golpayegan are drawn with coordinates (lon/lat discs).
